title: Safety Watchman: proactive rollback decisioning and state harmonization for config changes
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Summary: Build an autonomous "Watchman" service that decides and safely executes rollbacks for runtime configuration changes (batching, caching, kernel selection, routing policies) while reconciling desired vs observed deployment state. The goal is to reduce Mean Time To Remediate (MTTR) for config-induced regressions (latency, error rate, cost spikes) without blocking safe experiments.

Background: We frequently roll runtime configs (batch/window_size, KV cache TTLs, scheduling hints). Some changes expose regressions that only appear under production traffic profiles (tail latency, token cost). We need a system that can: 1) detect harmful config deltas, 2) decide whether to auto-rollback or reduce exposure, 3) reconcile cluster state to a safe baseline, and 4) provide clear audit trails and dry-run simulation for engineers.

Scope & Non-Goals: Scope includes configuration changes that are applied via the control plane (runtime flags, model routing policies, autoscaling knobs, batching/caching params). Non-goals: replacing manual change approvals or expanding to model weights/version rollouts in this phase.

Key signals & triggers: error-rate (5xx) spike > X% vs baseline, p95 latency degradation > Y ms sustained for Z minutes, token-cost/unit increase > 30% outside expected pattern, deployment-state mismatch (control-plane says applied but nodes report older state), failed canary probes, negative quality/regression alerts from evals linked to the change. Signals are weighted into a Safety Score.

Decision logic & guardrails: - Safety Score combines signal strength, customer impact, traffic fraction, and recent rollback history. - Thresholds for automated rollback are conservative (high-confidence) and require either: (a) two orthogonal signals (latency + 5xx) OR (b) single catastrophic signal with high customer impact. - For intermediate scores, Watchman implements staged mitigation: reduce traffic % to previous stable variant, switch to compatible model variant (lower cost but tested), or set conservative batching/caching config. - All automated actions create an in-app incident, send PagerDuty + Slack, and open a brief audit in the Console with 'why' reasoning.

State reconciliation: - Desired-state is the last known-good config (tagged and immutable). - Apply is tracked with per-change idempotent ops and sequence numbers. - Reconciliation loop periodically compares node-local effective config vs control-plane desired config; if drift detected, Watchman can either reapply desired config or isolate nodes for remediation. - A stabilization window and hysteresis prevents thrashing: once a rollback occurs, automatic re-applies to the same config are blocked for a cooldown.

Dry-run & simulation: Before auto-apply/rollback, Watchman can run a shadow-apply (traffic mirroring) on a small sample to compute expected cost/latency delta using historical traces and the batching/caching estimator. The estimator accounts for KV cache warmup penalties and batching throughput changes.

Observability & audit: Expose per-change dashboard with: signals timeline, Safety Score evolution, decision rationale, simulated vs observed cost delta, and runbook links. All actions are logged with operator, change-id, and GitHub PR or Confluence design reference.

Implementation plan (high level): Phase 1: signal collection + decision engine prototype (feature flags) + simple auto-rollback on binary catastrophic rules. Phase 2: integrate simulation, staged mitigations, reconciliation loop and cooldown/hysteresis. Phase 3: Console UI, runbook automation, and operator overrides + policy-as-code.

Trade-offs: Aggressive auto-rollback reduces outage time but risks reverting benign experiments; we mitigate via conservative thresholds, two-signal rules, and staged mitigation. Simulations improve confidence but add complexity and potential false negatives for rare tails.
acceptance_criteria: Watchman computes a Safety Score from at least 3 production signals and exposes it in a test dashboard
An automated rollback event triggers for a synthetic catastrophic scenario (integration test) and the system records full audit details
Staged mitigation (traffic percentage reduction) can be executed automatically and verified in canary traffic tests
Reconciliation loop detects drift within 2 minutes in lab tests and either re-applies desired config or marks node as quarantined
Dry-run simulation produces cost and latency delta estimates within 15% of observed for recorded rollbacks (benchmarked)
Unit tests and e2e harness for decision engine and reconciliation loop are present; code review + security review sign-off
Runbook and console expose a one-click operator override and 'undo' that safely lifts automated blocks
